title: Key custody onboarding & access signoff playbook for Private deployments
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Purpose: Define a concise, actionable playbook and sign-off checklist for onboarding customer-managed key custody and admin/RBAC access during Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. This ticket consolidates PRD clarifications, acceptance criteria, and the cross-functional sign-offs required before a Private deployment can be marked Ready for Customer Onboarding.

Context: Customers choose Private deployments when they require control of cryptographic keys (CMEK/HSM) and tighter audit controls. Past rollouts showed ambiguity around who approves key-rotation procedures, the exact audit evidence required, and how SSO/SAML assertions map to RBAC roles. The playbook will remove ambiguity and reduce go/no-go back-and-forth during customer onboarding and compliance assessments.
requirements: SSO/SAML: Verify SAML 2.0 metadata exchange, automatic user/role provisioning (SCIM optional), and assertion attribute mapping to Redwood RBAC roles.
RBAC: Define minimum viable role set (Admin, Security-Admin, Operator, Viewer) and document required privileges and allowed actions for each role in Private deployments.
KMS/HSM integration: Outline supported KMS providers, required key policies, customer HSM acceptance criteria, and failover behavior for key unavailability.
Audit logs: Specify events and retention window (default 365 days), required fields (actor, timestamp, resource, action, request_id), and examples of evidence to satisfy enterprise auditors.
Key lifecycle: Provide onboarding steps for key injection, verification, test rotation, emergency rotation, and decommissioning with observable artifacts for each step.
Operational playbooks: Include runbooks for lost-key scenarios, emergency key revocation, and rolling back to Redwood-managed keys with minimal downtime.
Acceptance artifacts: List of artifacts (signed runbook, integration test logs, GitHub PR for infra-as-code, SOC-type checklist entries) that must be produced and attached before signoff.

acceptance_criteria:
1) SAML integration: A test tenant completes SAML handshake and logs show successful assertion mapping to at least one RBAC role.
2) RBAC: Demo of least-privilege setup for Operator role with recorded session and policy snippet.
3) KMS/HSM: Key injection test succeeds; test rotation completes and application continues serving with no data loss; logs and rotation audit recorded.
4) Audit logs: Sample audit bundle demonstrating required fields and retention export/import runs.
5) Runbooks & artifacts: All items in the signoff checklist attached to the ticket.
6) Stakeholder signoff: Security, SRE, Product, and Enterprise Sales each provide explicit approval (signed checklist entries).
signoff_checklist: Security (Lead): Confirm KMS/HSM provider compatibility and approve key lifecycle runbook.
SRE/Infra: Validate rotation test and emergency-rotation procedure in staging; attach logs and incident playbook.
Product (PM): Confirm acceptance criteria satisfied and customer-facing docs updated.
DevRel/Docs: Publish onboarding guide and example terraform/ansible snippets to the private-deploy repo.
Enterprise Sales/AE: Confirm contract language aligns with key custody statements and support SLAs.
Legal/Privacy: Confirm that audit log retention/exports meet jurisdictional requirements for the customer (if specified).
Ops: Confirm monitoring alerts for key-unavailability and automated fallback are in place.
testing_plan: Define a dedicated private-deploy staging tenant to run the end-to-end scenario: (a) ingest customer SAML metadata, (b) provision roles via RBAC mapping, (c) inject a test key into target KMS with a test policy, (d) run rotation script, (e) verify streaming inference continues and audit events are emitted. Save all logs to an artifacts bucket and attach SHA-256 checksums to the ticket.
rollout_notes: Rollout will occur in two phases: Phase A (Internal validation) — runbook validation and SRE stress tests; Phase B (Pilot customer onboarding) — one pilot customer with dedicated SRE on-call and 24-48h observation window. Rollback criteria: failed rotation test or missing audit evidence. Communicate schedule to AE and Support 72 hours in advance.
